newsitem.title: USA: Senate approves annual intelligence bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate approves annual intelligence bill.

text.p: The Senate approved an annual intelligence bill Tuesday that would move toward streamlining U.S. intelligence on the spread of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons around the world.

It approved the annual spending authorisation bill for a dozen U.S. intelligence agencies including the Central Intelligence Agency by voice vote. The amount is secret but has been reported to be about $28 billion.
The Senate bill must be compromised with a House version for Congress's final approval.
The Senate bill would establish a presidential commission to assess the U.S. government's ability to combat the spread of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons around the world.
Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Arlen Specter, a Pennsylvnia Republican, has said too many federal agencies are involved in the effort and their work is not well coordinated.
The bill would also give the director of central intelligence, now John Deutch, more control over major intelligence agencies by giving him a strong voice in appointing chiefs of the agencies.
